column1: # dev-ports.tsv — the single source of truth for every TCP/UDP port this
# repository's development and test tooling binds on a developer's machine.
# T-1807-bug-02. Read docs/testing/port-registry.md before adding a row.
# Why this file exists: four times in one phase, two independent pieces of
# this repo's own tooling reached for the same port and produced a failure
# that looked like a product defect. The fourth time was the fix for the
# third: T-1807-bug-01 moved packaging/test/upgrade-service.sh to 61007
# "chosen outside the entire N8006/N8007 family" — and 61007 is the
# phys-collapse e2e stack's own vnproxd. Commit 9047685 had to move it
# again. A doc table would not have caught that; a test that reads this
# file and refuses an unregistered or double-claimed port does.
# Format: port <TAB> proto <TAB> owner <TAB> binder <TAB> purpose
#   port    decimal, 1-65535
#   proto   tcp | udp
#   owner   short stable label, unique per port
#   binder  repo-relative path of the file that binds it (the authority)
#   purpose one line, why this port and not another
# Consumed by:
#   internal/devports          (Go: parse + the make-check enforcement test)
#   packaging/test/lib/ports.sh (shell: ports_require_free preflight)
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.

T-2801. The demo-mode e2e stack's vnproxd (`vnproxd --demo --config testdata/demo.toml`). It has NO NNN006 sibling on purpose: a demo daemon's PVE mock runs in-process over a transport with no dialer (internal/demo/transport.go), so there is no second process and no second port to claim.

T-2802. The hosted-demo e2e stack's vnproxd (`vnproxd --demo --public-demo --config testdata/demo-public.toml`). Like 24007 it has NO NNN006 sibling — its synthetic cluster runs in-process — and it is a second daemon rather than a second flag on 24007 because the two answer the same routes differently: 200 "would have" there, 403 at the edge here.

Real systemd service under podman --network=host, so it shares the host's port namespace. Moved here from 61007 by 9047685 after colliding with vnproxd-physcollapse — the incident this registry exists to prevent.
